answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller to lock a bond before accepting work, whether it sells comet forecasts, walnut price data, or fable illustrations. Selection is weighted by bonded stake, so splitting one bond among a thousand identities gives no extra chance of winning jobs. Payments stay in escrow, and a cryptographically proven breach forfeits the seller’s bond. An attacker must tie up more capital to gain influence and risks losing it when cheating.
